territorial_scope.description: Applies in Denmark, with persons in scope defined by reference to Article 2(1)(a)-(f) of the AI Act; excluded from the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

evidence.quote: Loven gælder ikke for Færøerne og Grønland.

summary.short: Proposed Danish act supplementing EU AI Regulation 2024/1689. Designates market-surveillance and contact authorities, gives them inspection, order, temporary-ban and online-blocking powers over AI providers, deployers, distributors and online-interface owners, requires registration of certain AI safety components, and sets fines. Effective the day after promulgation.
summary.long: The bill, introduced on 7 October 2026 by the Danish research, education and digitalisation minister, supplements Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) for Denmark. It designates the Agency for Digitalisation as central contact point and coordinator of market-surveillance authorities, and makes the Danish Courts Administration a market-surveillance authority for courts' own use of AI systems. The minister may set by regulation which authorities act as national competent or market-surveillance authorities. Market-surveillance authorities may require information, sample AI systems, enter premises and issue orders requiring warnings, halting marketing, corrective action, withdrawal or recall. They may impose temporary bans on supplying an AI system that poses a risk. Owners of online interfaces may be ordered to change, remove or warn against content referring to non-compliant AI systems; blocking requires a court ruling. AI systems intended as safety components in critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or water, gas, heating and electricity supply must be registered with the Agency. Providers must keep certain information for five years after their AI system is placed on the market or put into service. Listed violations of AI Act provisions and of this act are punishable by fines, with legal persons liable under the Criminal Code; the limitation period is five years. Fines may be settled by summary penalty notice. The act enters into force the day after publication and repeals Act No. 467 of 14 May 2025. It does not apply to the Faroe Islands or Greenland.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no monetary, size, volume or other numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Numbers present are procedural or retention periods, not thresholds: 4 weeks appeal period (§ 3(4)); 3 months before a new request may be filed after a rejected request to lift a blocking order (§ 11(4)); 5-year record retention (§ 5(3)); 5-year limitation period (§ 17(4)). Article and paragraph numbers of the AI Act are cross-references only.
